title: Laying encaustic cement floor tiles in a geometric pattern
subtitle: Set out and lay handmade pigmented cement floor tiles in a patterned floor with a thin-bed adhesive
excerpt: How to lay encaustic cement tiles in a geometric floor pattern. Covers setting out the pattern, laying with cement-based thin-bed adhesive, grouting with a matching coloured grout, and sealing with a penetrating sealer.
sourceNotes: Traditional Moroccan and Victorian tile laying practice. Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced).

glossaryTerms.definition: An unglazed cement-bodied floor tile in which the coloured pattern is formed in the surface layer using pigmented cement pressed into a metal mould. The pattern is integral to the tile, not applied on top. Encaustic tiles are porous and must be sealed after laying. Victorian hallway and kitchen floor tiles are the classic UK application.

A cement-based tile adhesive applied as a thin, even layer (typically 3 to 6 mm) to the substrate, with the tile pressed into the adhesive. Used for all floor tiles laid over a firm, level screed or concrete base. Contrasted with a thick sand-and-cement mortar bed, which is used for very heavy stone or when levelling is needed.

content.text: over a level, primed concrete or screed base. Their porous surface absorbs adhesive from the back, so full back-coverage is critical. The pattern layout must be set out carefully before any adhesive goes down.
Sort and seal the tiles before laying

Encaustic tiles vary slightly in tone between manufacturing batches. Open all the boxes and blend tiles from different boxes across the floor to average out any colour variation. Apply a single coat of penetrating tile sealer to the face of each tile before laying. This provisional seal prevents adhesive and grout from staining the tile surface during installation. The final sealing comes after grouting.

Find the centre of the room by snapping chalk lines between the midpoints of opposite walls. Dry-lay the complete geometric pattern from the centre to all four walls to check the layout, the position of cut tiles at each wall, and the visual balance of the overall design. Adjust the starting point so that cut tiles at doorways and visible walls are as large as possible. Mark the reference lines on the floor with a pencil before taking the dry-lay up.
Apply adhesive and lay the tiles

Spread a thin, even layer of cement-based tile adhesive (recommended by the tile manufacturer for porous tiles) over an area of approximately 0.5 square metres using the flat face of the plasterers trowel. Back-butter each tile with a thin skim of adhesive using the filling knife, covering the full back face. Press the tile firmly onto the adhesive, aligning to the chalk lines. Check level with the spirit level after every three or four tiles. Work from the centre of the room outward in quarters, maintaining the pattern geometry.

Allow the adhesive to cure for at least 24 hours. Use an unsanded coloured grout matched to the tile joint colour specified in the pattern design. Apply the grout over the tile surface using a filling knife, pressing it firmly into the joints. Wipe excess from the tile faces with a damp sponge before it dries. A second wipe with a clean damp cloth removes the haze. Do not use the floor for 48 hours after grouting.

Once the grout has cured fully (allow five to seven days), apply two coats of penetrating tile sealer to the whole floor including the joints. The sealer closes the pores in the cement tile body and prevents oil, water, and food staining the surface. Reapply the sealer annually in high-traffic areas.

attrs.symptom: Grout stains the tile surface and will not clean off
attrs.cause: The provisional sealer was not applied before laying, or grout was left too long on the surface.
attrs.fix: Use a specialist cement grout haze remover (dilute acidic cleaner) following the manufacturer's instructions. Test on a hidden tile first.

attrs.symptom: Pattern joints do not align across the floor
attrs.cause: The chalk reference lines were not followed closely enough, or tile dimensions varied slightly.
attrs.fix: Encaustic tiles are handmade and not perfectly consistent in size. Use 2 mm spacers throughout and check alignment back to the chalk lines every four to five tiles.
